metadata.title: Silent Failures
metadata.purpose: Provenance Gatekeeper development log, Week 4 — the final architecture: a persistent SQLite audit trail and an outbound webhook alarm that make intercepted hallucinations permanent and loud instead of ephemeral.

beats.narration_text: I am Onkar Bhujbal, a software engineer. Intercepting an A.I. hallucination is useless if the system forgets it happened a millisecond later. An orchestrator without a memory is just a black box. This week we finalized the Provenance Gatekeeper by building a persistent tracking database and an automated alerting system — to make A.I. failures loud, and permanent.

beats.narration_text: The final architecture operates on two principles: the audit trail, and the alarm. First, every claim the Gatekeeper evaluates is written to a local SQLite database — an immutable ledger of the model's accuracy over time. Second, if it detects a magnitude or directional error, it immediately fires an outbound webhook to notify human operators.

props.command: Send one false financial claim through n8n to the /verify endpoint, and show me what the tracking log and the alert channel each receive.

beats.authoring_note: ASK → RESULT pair: B03 is the ask, B04 is the result (ASK→RESULT LAW).

beats.narration_text: Here is the pipeline in action. When our n8n orchestrator passes a false financial claim to the FastAPI webhook, the evaluation layer flags it as a failure. Instantly a new row is committed to the SQLite tracking log, detailing the exact variance. Simultaneously, a webhook pushes a critical alert to our messaging platform — exposing the hallucination before it can propagate.

beats.narration_text: So why not just rely on n8n's own execution logs? Because workflow logs are ephemeral, and they are painful to query for analytics. With a dedicated relational database we can prove, mathematically, how often the underlying model lies, which type of error it favours, and whether its reliability degrades over time.

beats.narration_text: So audit the system. Run this SQLite command in your terminal to see the permanent record of every claim the model attempted to push through the Gatekeeper. You cannot fix a model you do not track.
beats.new_visual_element: The query the viewer runs against their own ledger

the TASK line lands: query the immutable ledger
the follow-up query lands last — the one that turns a log into a metric

props.title: audit.sh
props.code:
sqlite3 gatekeeper_logs.db \
  "SELECT generated_claim, variance_type
   FROM evaluation_logs;"

# TASK: query the immutable ledger.

# Then the query that matters:
#   SELECT variance_type, COUNT(*)
#   FROM evaluation_logs
#   GROUP BY variance_type;
#
# That is your model's error profile.

beats.authoring_note: The GROUP BY follow-up is the reel's addition: the script's command dumps rows, but Scene 4 claims the ledger yields an error profile — and that claim needs the aggregate query to be true.

beats.narration_text: And once that table has a few hundred rows in it, here is the prompt worth running. Hand a model your variance counts and ask it which error type your system is worst at, and what a fix would have to change. The ledger stops being a log the moment it starts answering questions.
